# Build discrete swept shadow along light-to-object direction, expand by one cell to model penumbra
from scipy.ndimage import binary_dilation
shadow=np.zeros_like(g,dtype=bool)
for i in range(1,n+1):
    pts=np.argwhere(lab==i)
    cr,cc=pts.mean(axis=0)
    dr=cr; dc=cc-19
    # normalize approximate direction using dominant sign / slope
    # represent ray step to keep slopes: use integer direction reduced by rounded centroid
    gr,gc=round(cr),round(cc-19)
    import math
    div=math.gcd(abs(gr),abs(gc)) or 1
    sr,sc=gr//div,gc//div
    if sr==0 and sc==0: continue
    for k in range(1,30):
        rr=pts[:,0]+k*sr; co=pts[:,1]+k*sc
        valid=(rr>=0)&(rr<20)&(co>=0)&(co<20)
        if not valid.any(): break
        shadow[rr[valid],co[valid]]=1
# dilate one step for thick shadow
sh2=binary_dilation(shadow,structure=np.ones((3,3))) & (g==8)
out=g.copy(); out[sh2]=7
print('\n'.join(' '.join(map(str,row)) for row in out))

def line_cells(r0,c0,r1,c1):
 # integer Bresenham inclusive
 pts=[]; dx=abs(c1-c0); sx=1 if c0<c1 else -1; dy=-abs(r1-r0); sy=1 if r0<r1 else -1; err=dx+dy
 r,c=r0,c0
 while True:
  pts.append((r,c))
  if (r,c)==(r1,c1):break
  e2=2*err
  if e2>=dy:err+=dy;c+=sx
  if e2<=dx:err+=dx;r+=sy
 return pts
